title: When God Descends with Men to Dwell
description: When God Descends with Men to Dwell in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Hosea Ballou wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 289 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Blessings of Christ's Universal Reign”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When God de-scends with men to dwell, And all cre-a-tion makes a-new, What tongue can half the won-ders tell? What eye the daz-zling glo-ries view?

lines: When God descends with men to dwell,
And all creation makes anew,
What tongue can half the wonders tell?
What eye the dazzling glories view?
Zion, the desolate, again
Shall see her lands with roses bloom;
And Carmel's mount, and Sharon's plain,
Shall yield their spices and perfume.
Celestial streams shall gently flow;
The wilderness shall joyful be;
Lilies on parchéd ground shall grow;
And gladness spring on every tree;
The weak be strong, the fearful bold,
The deaf shall hear, the dumb shall sing,
The lame shall walk, the blind behold;
And joy through all the earth shall ring.
Monarchs and slaves shall meet in love;
Old pride shall die, and meekness reign, —
When God descends from worlds above,
To dwell with men on earth again.

licence: Public domain: Hosea Ballou died in 1852.
credits: Words by Hosea Ballou (1771–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
